items.text: Fars reported that Melika Azizi, one of the detainees of the December 1404 protests in Masal county, has been sentenced to 6 months of imprisonment. Fars denied the news of a death sentence for her.
A video shows a student tearing images of Ruhollah Khomeini from their textbooks and calling him the cause of "impoverishing" the Iranian people.

Sri Lankan officials announced they moved 40 Iranian sailors from 19 ships ashore due to urgent need for medical care. According to the officials, the sailors returned to Iran after receiving medical services. Meanwhile, dozens of Iranian oil tankers have been stranded in Asian waters following the US naval blockade.

Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, reacted to the meeting of senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan in Tehran, saying Saudi Arabia has caused significant damage to Iran and Iran is a creditor to them. He accused Saudi Arabia of trying to overthrow the Islamic Republic and said the country must reconsider its past policies and adjust its relations with the Islamic Republic. Rezaei also said the Islamic Republic has taken steps to establish a new security system in the region and the resistance axis is forming a model called mosaic security.

Esmaeil Baqaei, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic, reacted to Benjamin Netanyahu's threats by saying these threats are futile and a sign of desperation. He added that these threats only damage the credibility of the threateners among the public opinion in the region and Iran.

Jude Bellingham, the English midfielder of Real Madrid, played a key role in his team's 2-1 victory over Barcelona with a spectacular move in the 87th minute of El Clasico. This technical move drew widespread admiration from football fans and reactions on social media. Real Madrid defeated Barcelona 2-1 with goals from Kylian Mbappe and the cooperation of Bellingham and Camavinga.

A video received by Iran International shows that a group of Iranians residing in the UK held a ceremony for the birthday anniversary of Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi in the city of Sheffield on Sunday, 3 Aban.

The Court of Appeal confirmed the five-year prison sentence of Soheil Arabi, a blogger, on charges of "assembly and collusion to commit a crime against national security." He was also banned from social media activities for two years. The court cited a report from the Tehran Intelligence Organization of the IRGC, claiming Arabi had connections with "foreign financial networks" and encouraged people to "subversive actions."

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, evaluated the visit of senior military and security officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan to Tehran as important in the current critical situation. He said these countries primarily seek to secure their national interests, and Saudi Arabia also tries to prevent escalation of tensions and the outbreak of war. According to Kazemian, this visit may involve conveying military and security warnings to the Islamic Republic.

Jalal Hashemi, chairman of the board of the retired employees association of Homa Airlines, stated that two retired employees of the company abandoned their treatment and died in the past two to three weeks due to inability to pay hospital costs. Hashemi said the average salary of Homa retirees is about 27 million tomans and health insurance services have been cut due to lack of financial resources.

On the eve of the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony to be held on Monday, October 26 in London, the competition for the most prestigious individual football award remains uncertain. Harry Kane, Lamin Yamal, and Kylian Mbappe are the main contenders, but each has weaknesses in their past season records. The Goal website wrote that unlike previous editions, no nominee has indisputable reasons to win the Ballon d'Or.

Street protests continue in several European cities focusing on rising living costs, housing crisis, and government economic policies. In France, Emmanuel Macron is going to Marseille to assess the restoration of public order, and protests have also been held in Prague, Lisbon, and Barcelona.

Videos received by Iran International show the memorial of Alireza Raeisi at his workplace, a poultry shop. A source close to Alireza Raeisi's family said that five knives belonging to his workplace were used as evidence against him in court.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the scope of possible US operations in the region depends on Washington's goals; from limited attacks on Iran's missile and nuclear capabilities to broader operations aimed at forcing the government to surrender or regime change. He also mentioned the possibility of attacks on military infrastructure and command centers and ground operations in the regime change scenario.

Fadahossein Maleki, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said Iran will achieve whatever it wants and is not far from using nuclear knowledge. He warned that in case of war, the Islamic Republic will target sites in Arab countries of the region and also mobile targets in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman. These statements were made in an interview with Didban Iran.
On Monday, 4 Aban, a group of retired telecommunications workers in the cities of Kermanshah and Isfahan held a protest gathering demanding attention to their demands.

Nearly a year has passed since the death of Sina Ghaemi, a well-known Iranian sports coach. His family recently commemorated his first birthday anniversary in his absence. Sina Ghaemi died in a car accident in Nigeria last Dey month.

The detention order for 12 citizens linked to the 'Qaleh Chenan' case has been extended. These individuals face charges including 'waging war against God' and 'rebellion.' The hearing originally scheduled for the 1st of Aban has been postponed for one month.

Messages received by Iran International indicate a shortage of flour, closure of some bakeries, and an increase in bread prices in various cities in Iran. Citizens and bakers say that the cut or delay in flour supply has disrupted the activities of independent bakeries and producers of large and semi-large breads. This issue has heightened concerns about bread supply.

Israel's Channel 12 reported a severe disagreement between Benjamin Netanyahu, the Prime Minister, and Eyal Zamir, the Chief of Staff, over the execution of a military order that might lead to a new confrontation with Iran. Zamir refused to execute the order and requested further reviews and a written legal authorization. Netanyahu called the report baseless and said there is no disagreement.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Speaker of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, accused Lana Nusseibeh, an Emirati diplomat and candidate for the UN Secretary-General position, of trying to pave the diplomatic path for the "Greater Israel project" and "whitewashing the genocide in Gaza." Ali Al Nuaimi, head of the Defense, Homeland, and Foreign Affairs Commission of the UAE Federal National Council, responded by accusing the Islamic Republic of "exporting instability" and said Ghalibaf's rhetoric reflects a destructive mentality.

The Deputy Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council confirmed the visit of senior officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey to Tehran on 4 Aban for a joint meeting and regional coordination. Khalid bin Salman, Asim Munir, and Ibrahim Kalin will participate in this meeting with Mohsen Rezaei. This visit was previously reported by Reuters.
Ali Haji, a teachers' union activist in Jolfa, was summoned and interrogated by the intelligence department of Jolfa on 25 Mehr. The summons was related to his activities on social media.

Jalal Hashemi, chairman of the board of the Retirees Association of Iran Air, reported livelihood and medical problems for about 13,000 retirees and pensioners of the company. He stated that Iran Air cut the monthly welfare allowance for retirees in Esfand 1404 due to war consequences, and the retirees' medical fund has a 400 billion toman deficit. Also, two retirees have died in the past two to three weeks due to inability to pay hospital costs.

The official Iraqi news agency reported that an arrest warrant was issued for Mustafa Daair Abdulhassan, head of the Maysan provincial council in Iraq, due to threats of disobedience and blocking roads if the border crossing with Iran is not opened. The Iraqi Prime Minister's office had filed a complaint against Abdulhassan because of these threats. Abdulhassan had threatened to block all roads if the Al-Shaib border crossing with Iran, known as Chazabeh, was not opened.

The Olympic Council of Asia announced that the 6th Asian Indoor and Martial Arts Games hosted by Riyadh have been postponed due to recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The competition will be held from April 8 to 19, 1406 [Gregorian: 2027-04-08] in Riyadh. More than 4,500 athletes from over 45 National Olympic Committees are expected to participate in the games.

The Afghanistan Athletics Federation stated that since Ehsan Haddadi's presidency of the Iran Athletics Federation, conditions have become more difficult for Afghan migrant athletes. Masoud Majnoon, advisor to the Afghanistan Athletics Federation, said Afghan athletes have difficulty obtaining permission to train and compete, and requests from Afghan officials are not answered. Iran International reports that Afghan athletes residing in Iran face serious obstacles to participating in official competitions and using training facilities.

The sister of Alireza Sepahi, an executed protester, shared a photo of him in court and wrote about his dazed look and innocence. She said she does not know what her brother was thinking or fearing moments before his death. Sepahi's sister added that no one should face death with such a look full of questions and silent grief.

Alam Azizi, a citizen from Qasr-e Qand and one of the detainees of the December 1404 protests, remains in judicial uncertainty and is being held in Zahedan prison despite more than 9 months having passed since his arrest.

Tehran's prosecutor announced charges against the organizers of the "Art Fair Tehran" art exhibition for not observing "legal and religious standards." The ticket sales website and the organizer's social media account were blocked, and the accused were summoned to provide explanations. The fifth edition of this exhibition was held from October 20 to November 1 at the Iran Mall International Exhibition Center.

Houshang Hasenyari, a Middle East and military affairs expert, referring to the visits of Saudi Arabian, Pakistani, and Turkish officials to Iran, said: The conflicting interests of these countries with each other and with the Islamic Republic make it impossible to reach an agreement to prevent the spread of war, curb Houthi attacks, and establish regional security arrangements.

Videos received by Iran International show that a group of students from Gorgan University of Agricultural Sciences and Natural Resources on Tuesday, 4 Aban, protested the poor quality of food by placing food trays on the ground and gathering.

Ata Hosseinian, an economic journalist in the energy sector, said the news wave about combating fuel smuggling, based on past years' experience, is a prelude to an increase in gasoline prices. According to him, new fuel supply restrictions may stem from the government's concern about gasoline shortages in case of war and attacks on infrastructure.

The price of each kilogram of chicken has risen from about 280,000 tomans to 350,000 tomans within one week. ILNA reports that the minimum daily wage of workers is only enough to buy a small one-and-a-half-kilogram chicken. Labor activist Faramarz Tofighi estimates that the cost of the minimum subsistence basket for worker households may have reached 100 million tomans by the end of Mehr.

A senior official of the Islamic Republic told Reuters that Iranian officials will not discuss their nuclear program in the talks on Tuesday with members of the Makkah Pact in Tehran. The official said the US must first meet Tehran's conditions for a permanent end to the war against the Islamic Republic. Representatives of the Makkah Pact countries met with Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran to discuss reducing regional tensions and encouraging dialogue.

The Deputy of Social and Cultural Traffic of Tehran's Rahvar Police announced that since the beginning of the year 1405, 143 people have died in capital city accidents due to inattention ahead, accounting for 39% of all accident fatalities in Tehran. Additionally, 4,920 people have been injured in these incidents, making up 35% of all accident injuries.
A four-party meeting of the Islamic Republic, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia focusing on regional security and stability has started in Tehran.

Channel 12 Israel reported that Eyal Zamir, Chief of Staff of the Army, opposed Benjamin Netanyahu's intended action that could have led to an escalation of conflict with the Islamic Republic before the elections. CNN also reported that Donald Trump opposed Netanyahu's request to start military action against the Islamic Republic before the Israeli parliamentary elections. Netanyahu denied both reports.
According to the head of the Fire Department and Safety Services of Kermanshah Municipality, an explosion in a residential house in the Jafarabad neighborhood of Kermanshah left 10 injured.

A report was published about the collapse of the watchtowers of Rajaishahr Prison (Gohardasht), recalling six years of life in this prison. The report refers to the protests and strikes in 1393 in Evin Prison and the exile to Gohardasht Prison, addressing the harsh conditions of political prisoners and death row inmates there. It also mentions the bloody history of this prison and the fate of political prisoners in the 1980s.

A source close to Alireza Raeisi's family said five knives belonging to the poultry shop where he worked were used as evidence against him in court. Alireza Raeisi was arrested on 29 Dey and sentenced to death on charges of "enmity against God." His death sentence was carried out on 13 Mehr, and his body was buried without the family's knowledge in the deserts of Anarak in Isfahan province.

Hossein Boroujerdi, political deputy of the Qazvin province IRGC, said 250 American forces entered Isfahan but their operation failed due to what he called "divine help." Iranian armed forces were located 5 kilometers from the American forces, and one American plane had a technical issue upon landing, causing their retreat. The incident happened because of noise from attempts to free the plane.

The Supreme National Security Council of the Islamic Republic of Iran has instructed the media not to provide analysis either in support of or against the "Mecca Agreement." This directive was issued simultaneously with the visit of senior defense and security officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey to Tehran. The Tehran meeting will discuss regional security, the consequences of US and Israeli military attacks on Iran, and aid to the people of Palestine and Lebanon.

Hassan Golshannejad, a detainee linked to the protests of Dey 1404 in Mashhad, has been sentenced to death by the Fifth Branch of the Revolutionary Court. The sentence was issued on the charge of "operational action in favor of Israel" and was communicated to him today. The case is related to his participation in the protests of Dey 1404.

Iranian state media reported that Mohsen Rezaei and Abbas Araghchi welcomed officials from three member countries of the Makkah Pact in Tehran. The meeting was held at Pakistan's proposal and topics such as regional cooperation and US and Israeli aggression against Iran are on the agenda. Iran's Supreme National Security Council instructed media not to analyze the Makkah agreement and emphasized regional cooperation for security.

Luis Inacio Lula da Silva, president of Brazil, won the second round of elections defeating Flavio Bolsonaro for a fourth presidential term. His supporters celebrated until early Monday in Brasilia. Bolsonaro has not accepted the election results and announced he will challenge them.

According to information received by Iran International, Hassan Golshan Nejad, a 36-year-old resident of Mashhad, was arrested on the fifth of Esfand last year and his preliminary death sentence was announced to him on the fourth of Aban in court. He has 10 days to appeal this sentence. The charges against him include waging war against God, assembly and collusion, insulting the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Republic, participating in Prince Reza Pahlavi's call, cooperating with the Israeli government, and damaging public property.

Videos released show that a group of retired telecommunications workers gathered on Tuesday, 4 Aban, in the cities of Isfahan, Tehran, and Kermanshah, shouting: "The Imam's Command Headquarters has taken our rights."

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said on Tuesday, 4 Aban, before his trip to Russia that Tehran-Moscow relations are expanding and he will discuss the development of bilateral cooperation with Vladimir Putin. He emphasized the necessity of free trade and energy transfer worldwide and called for expanding trade exchanges using national currencies. Pezeshkian also said Tehran's foreign policy aims to expand multilateralism, not unilateralism.

Today, on the fourth of Aban, four years have passed since the fortieth-day ceremony of Mahsa Zhina Amini, when a large crowd went to Aichi Cemetery in Saqqez, during which some citizens were killed, injured, or arrested. Simultaneously, images sent from over 30 cities in Iran, including Tehran, showed the spread of protests. Iran International extensively covered these nationwide protests, and its journalists share their experiences covering the events and memorable images that remain after four years.

Reuters reported that Hezbollah Lebanon, after receiving tens of millions of dollars in financial aid from the Islamic Republic, has spent the past three months preparing for a possible resumption of war with Israel. The sources said Hezbollah has focused on preparing explosives and producing drones to attack Israeli positions. Hezbollah has also received tens of millions of dollars from the Islamic Republic to rebuild its military capabilities but faces challenges in rebuilding its command and control structures.

CNN, citing a US official, reported that the US military is prepared to start a major war with the Islamic Republic within 96 hours of receiving an order from Trump. This comes while senior security officials from three countries are traveling to Tehran to pursue final efforts for an agreement.
Nabi Sofi, a citizen from Shahin Dezh, was sentenced to three years and six months of imprisonment by the General and Revolutionary Court of this city.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing a protest poster installed on a wall in the city of Shahriar with the theme of overthrowing the Islamic Republic, addressing the regime leaders saying, "You will soon perish as well."
As the US midterm congressional elections approach, American officials have accused Canada of trying to influence these elections. Tensions between Washington and Ottawa have increased.

CNN, citing two US officials, reported that US forces in the Middle East are ready to launch a large-scale military operation against the Islamic Republic within 96 hours of receiving an order from Donald Trump. This report comes amid increasing media reports about the possibility of resuming war against the Islamic Republic.

The Director General of School Renovation in Qom announced that the province needs to build about 100 schools including 1100 classrooms to reach the national average of educational space per capita, and about 20% of educational spaces need to be demolished and rebuilt. He also said that due to the construction of more than 90,000 housing units and population growth, about two thousand more classrooms are needed to meet the required educational space.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, in an exclusive interview with Iran International, urged Iranians to stop paying taxes and to stockpile fuel before winter arrives. He predicted that Iran's economy will shrink by more than 25 percent by March 2027.

The film "A Little Light" directed by Ali Asgari continues its global screenings after participating in the competition section of the Venice Film Festival. Forouzan Jamshidnejad, an actress in the film, described her participation as a "tribute" to Iranian protesters and spoke about her experience of migration and freedom of acting outside Iran. The film was screened at festivals in Los Angeles, Chicago, London, Hamburg, and Zurich, and participated in the competition section of the Hamburg festival.

A defendant in a murder case in Malard was sentenced to death by the Criminal Court of Tehran Province. A request for retrial by a prisoner sentenced to death was rejected by the 10th branch of the Criminal Court One of Tehran Province. Additionally, a murder case in the judicial district of Kuhdasht was settled through reconciliation after the victim's family pardoned the death penalty.

Khalid bin Salman, Saudi Arabia's Defense Minister, Asim Munir, Pakistan's Army Chief, Ibrahim Kalin, head of Turkey's intelligence agency, and Mohsen Rezaee, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, concluded their four-party talks at Saadabad Palace in Tehran on Monday, 4 Aban. Riyadh had previously announced that representatives of the 'Mecca Joint Defense Agreement' traveled to Tehran as part of efforts to reduce tensions and strengthen dialogue.

A video sent to Iran International shows the poor condition of the Khadijeh Kobra dormitory in Dezful. According to a citizen who sent the video, they have complained multiple times about this situation but it has had no effect.

A number of workers on the Chabahar–Zahedan railway project reported not receiving two months of their wages, and about 20 of them were dismissed after a strike. Employees and retirees of the oil industry in Khuzestan have complained about disruptions in receiving medical services.

In three work accidents in the cities of Arak, Nahavand, and Ahvaz, two people died and one worker was rescued from under rubble. One of the deceased was a construction worker who fell into an elevator shaft, and the other was a 47-year-old man who was electrocuted while picking walnuts. Additionally, a member of the Qom city council reported the deaths of three street cleaners in traffic accidents over the past two months.

The New York Times reported that the US Army trained Apache attack helicopter pilots in Germany to intercept and shoot down drones similar to Iran-made Shahed drones. The exercise aimed to test the effectiveness of Apache helicopters against drone threats in new wars. Shahed drones, despite their low speed, have managed to bypass US air defense systems and have caused nearly all US casualties so far in the war with Iran.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, in an exclusive interview with Iran International, referring to the policy of 'economic exclusion' of Iran, said the economy of the Islamic Republic will shrink by more than 25 percent from March 2026 to March 2027.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International saying that the prices of food items are increasing every day in Iran and expressed hope that Netanyahu would become prime minister again and the Islamic Republic would be overthrown.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad said senior military and security officials from Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey simultaneously arrived in Tehran on Monday to hold closed-door talks with officials of the Islamic Republic. He added that this trip took place amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and increased military tensions between the Islamic Republic and the United States.

Alireza Dabir, head of the Wrestling Federation, said in an interview with IRIB about a clash with the organizers of the World Wrestling Championships: "The thugs and politicians know what I did." He claimed that the clash that occurred beside the mat yesterday caused referees to behave differently towards Iranian wrestlers on the last day of the Greco-Roman competition.

The Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that the visit of Khalid bin Salman, the country's Defense Minister, and representatives of the member countries of the Makkah Joint Defense Pact to Tehran was aimed at reducing tensions and supporting diplomatic solutions. This visit is part of ongoing efforts to encourage dialogue and achieve diplomatic solutions. It also supports the mediation efforts of Qatar and Pakistan.

Tractor football team lost 2-1 to Al Ain UAE in the third week of the Asian Elite League. Rabia scored at the 21st minute and Hossein Rahimi at the 70th minute for Al Ain, while Helilovic scored at the 55th minute for Tractor. Tractor stands twelfth in the West Asia table with only one point.
Mohsen Aghal, a citizen from Sarbaz County, remains in detention 11 days after his arrest, and his family has so far been unable to obtain information about his condition and whereabouts.

The official Ballon d'Or website published an article titled "Harry Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or" more than four hours before the official announcement. Similar articles about Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé, and Lionel Messi were also published on the website. It is still unclear whether these articles were published by mistake or not.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the Caspian Sea coast near the village of Mirud Babolsar in Mazandaran province, which is full of garbage.
The 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony will be held in London in a few hours with the presence of football stars; this ceremony has returned to London after 70 years.

The United Students channel reported that Ali Alirezaei, a mathematics student at Sharif University of Technology, has been sentenced to one year of definitive imprisonment. The Central Council of the Ministry of Science has sentenced this student to expulsion from the university and a five-year ban from studying at all universities. Alirezaei was previously sentenced on 23 Tir 1405 to three years in prison for "assembly and collusion with intent to act against national security" and one year for "propaganda activities against the regime."

Scott Bassett, the US Treasury Secretary, said in an exclusive interview with Iran International that it is unbelievable that a country with the third largest natural energy reserves in the world does not produce enough gasoline to meet domestic needs. He added that the government is unable to provide public services and advises people not to pay taxes. Bassett also told the people of Iran to prepare everything they need for winter and to think about storing fuel now.

Morteza Nemati, a suspended professor from Chamran University of Ahvaz, said that after multiple cases were filed against him in the past three years and he had repeatedly gone to court, a new case was recently filed against him for sympathizing with the family of the martyr Alireza Saidi, who was killed in the protests of Dey 1404.

Scott Busent, the US Treasury Secretary, said the US actions target the Iranian government, not the people, and that the US stands in full solidarity with the Iranian people. He added that as the economic situation in Iran worsens, the government's fear of the Iranian people increases. Busent also stated that the US wants to see a day when Iran flourishes again.

Fereshteh Pezeshk said Donald Trump's support for Benjamin Netanyahu does not mean that US policy depends on Netanyahu remaining prime minister. She added that military and security cooperation between Israel and the US against the Islamic Republic will continue even if the Israeli government changes. Pezeshk predicted that tensions could lead to more serious conflicts in the coming months.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the burning of the Islamic Republic flag in a city in Khuzestan province on the occasion of Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi's birthday.

Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury Department's sanctions targeting office, said Scott Bassett's statements about the results of the economic pressure campaign against the Islamic Republic indicate that sanctions and maritime and air blockade have had a significant impact. He added that some foreign companies that previously cooperated with the Islamic Republic in selling oil and petrochemical products have stopped their activities. Maleki emphasized that the Islamic Republic still relies on cryptocurrencies and land routes to circumvent sanctions, but these methods are costly and cannot replace maritime and air trade.

The result of the Israeli parliamentary elections is important not only for the people of that country but can also affect Iran's political equations and even the future of the Islamic Republic. Benjamin Netanyahu urged voters to vote for his party to, as he said, eliminate the threat of the Islamic Republic and the "Tehran axis of evil" forever. A conversation was held with Alireza Nourizadeh and Jamshid Barzegar about this issue.

Lamine Yamal won the best young male talent award for the third consecutive year and is also a candidate for the 2026 Ballon d'Or. Vicky Lopez, forward for Barcelona and the Spanish national team, won the best young female talent award for the second consecutive year. After receiving the award, Yamal said this is the third year he has won it and thanked his club and national team, while Lopez dedicated her award to her mother.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, advised the people of Iran not to pay taxes and to prepare for a possible shortage of heating fuel and gasoline in winter. He said the Islamic Republic cannot meet the people's needs and emphasized that the US government and military stand with the people of Iran. Bessent also reported an intensification of economic pressure on the Islamic Republic in the next eight weeks and confirmed that six European banks have been asked to provide information about financial activities related to Iran.

Farzin Nadimi said Israel's military doctrine has fundamentally changed after the October 7 attacks. He added that Israel now seeks to eliminate threats preemptively before they materialize. Nadimi also said if Eisenkot wins the elections, the new government might prioritize rebuilding military capabilities, but escalating threats from Tehran could keep direct confrontation policy in place.

Luis de la Fuente, coach of the Spanish national team who led the country to the World Cup victory, won the Best Men's Coach of the Year award. He said the award belongs to his entire team and thanked the Spanish Football Federation. Also, Pere Romeo, coach of Barcelona women's team, won the Best Women's Football Coach of the Year award.

Kata Kol, goalkeeper of Barcelona and the Spanish national team, won the best women's football goalkeeper award at the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony. Unai Simón, goalkeeper of Athletic Bilbao and the Spanish national team, received the best men's goalkeeper award. Both winners thanked their national teams and supporters.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, stated that the US is tracking and seizing digital currencies and funds taken abroad by officials of the Islamic Republic and their affiliates. Bessent said that all these funds are held in an escrow account because they belong to the people of Iran and must be returned to them.

At the 2026 Ballon d'Or ceremony, Barcelona won the Best Women's Club of the Year award, and Paris Saint-Germain won the Best Men's Club of the Year award. Ousmane Dembélé received the award on behalf of Paris Saint-Germain and thanked the club members and coach. Joan Laporta, Barcelona's president, thanked France Football and L'Équipe after receiving the Best Women's Club award.

Harry Kane, captain of the England national team and Bayern Munich, won the 2026 Best Male Forward award. Charline Coral, forward for Pachuca and the Mexico national team, won the 2026 Best Female Forward award. Coral said she is happy to be the first Mexican woman to receive this award and proud of Mexico's strong performance in women's football.

Alexia Putellas, captain of Barcelona and star of the Spanish national team, won the 2026 Women's Ballon d'Or and equaled Aitana Bonmatí's record by winning her third trophy. Putellas led Barcelona last season to victories in La Liga, the Copa del Rey, the Spanish Super Cup, and the UEFA Champions League. After winning the award, she said that any player present could have deserved it and expressed pride in her team.

Shahram Khaledi said Qatar is mediating to reach a temporary agreement between the US and the Islamic Republic, but Washington has kept the military option and sees itself in a superior position. Representatives of Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan are seeking guarantees about shipping security in the Strait of Hormuz and stopping Houthi attacks in talks with the Islamic Republic. Diplomatic negotiations and readiness for military action will continue in parallel for a long time.

Mohammad Ghaedi, a professor of international relations, said that Masoud Pezeshkian's trip to Moscow followed Sergey Lavrov's trip to Tehran, and Russia could play a role in nuclear negotiations between the Islamic Republic and the United States. According to him, the possible transfer of 400 kilograms of Iran's enriched uranium to Russia is one of the issues that could be raised in the negotiations. Ghaedi added that Moscow might use its relations with Tehran to gain concessions from Washington, especially regarding the Ukraine war.

Ehsan Daneshvar, a senior energy and environmental expert, said the water crisis in Iran is not only due to reduced rainfall but is the result of decades of mismanagement, wrong policies, and overconsumption of renewable water resources. He added that costly water transfer projects contribute to environmental destruction, dust expansion, and land subsidence. Daneshvar warned that this situation could lead to increased social tensions and migration and emphasized that development should be aligned with available water resources.

Harry Kane, captain of the England national team and Bayern Munich striker, won the 2026 Ballon d'Or and is the first English player in 25 years to receive this award. Kane scored 73 goals in club and national competitions in the 2025-26 season and has scored 156 goals in 158 games since joining Bayern Munich in 2023. He also led the England national team to their best World Cup result since 1966 and ranked fifth in the World Cup top scorers list.

CNN reported, citing two American officials, that US forces are ready to launch extensive attacks against Iran's energy infrastructure, military bases and nuclear facilities within 96 hours of an order by Donald Trump. Concurrently, American and Israeli sources said Benjamin Netanyahu sought a joint attack on Iran before the Israeli election, but Trump did not agree to the request.

Ahead of the Israeli parliamentary elections, Benjamin Netanyahu faces rivals who support continued pressure on the Islamic Republic but differ on how to confront it. Netanyahu has stated that confronting the nuclear and missile programs of the Islamic Republic and overthrowing the Iranian government are among his goals. Gadi Eizenkot, Naftali Bennett, and Itamar Ben-Gvir each have different views on military confrontation or pressure against the Islamic Republic.

Maariv newspaper reported, citing Israeli military sources, that tension has increased between the country's political officials and the Chief of Staff of the army, along with several senior military commanders. The army commanders have opposed overt Israeli Air Force flights in some Middle Eastern areas and warned that these flights could escalate security tensions. They are also concerned about the impact of these tensions on the parliamentary elections scheduled for next Tuesday.

Israel Hayom newspaper reported, citing diplomatic sources in Gulf countries, that Khalid bin Salman, Saudi Arabia's defense minister, traveled to Tehran aiming to reach a ceasefire with Yemen's Houthis. The proposal includes Saudi Arabia paying $1 billion to the Houthis via Tehran in exchange for stopping attacks. Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry described the trip as part of efforts to reduce tensions and support diplomatic mediation.

The New York Times, citing two informed diplomats, wrote that Qatar is drafting a plan for a five-day agreement between the Islamic Republic and the United States, which includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz, lifting the blockade of Iranian ports, and obtaining a nuclear concession from Tehran. The main obstacle to the agreement is disagreement over the timing of the commitments. Mediators are also trying to convince the Islamic Republic to give a concession on its nuclear program in the first phase of the agreement.

On Monday, 4 Aban 1405, less than 24 hours before the start of voting in the Israeli general elections, a large billboard in Tel Aviv showed Benjamin Netanyahu alongside Donald Trump. Netanyahu spoke of Trump's support and indicated that if victorious, the two leaders could resume war with the Islamic Republic. Voting on Tuesday, 5 Aban is the first election after Hamas attacks on October 7, 2023, and polls show the Likud party losing seats.

Donald Trump said in a speech in Mississippi that a short ceasefire was established in the war with the Islamic Republic, which he considered a waste of time. He added that this ceasefire allowed some ships to enter and that oil prices are now lower.

Israel's parliamentary elections will be held on Tuesday, October 27, the country's first elections since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023. Benjamin Netanyahu's continued presence in power faces competition from centrist rivals in these elections. The final vote count is likely to be completed by October 30, and the official results will be announced on November 4, 2026.

Jonathan Schaech, a Middle East analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said the threat of the Islamic Republic in Israel is a vital issue and agreed upon by a wide range of political and security currents. He said that even if Gadi Eisenkot wins the election, there will be no significant change in Israel's policy towards the Islamic Republic, but the method of pursuing this policy and the approach to regime change in Tehran may differ.

Kamyar Behrang, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Trump and Netanyahu have entered a stage where negotiating with the Islamic Republic no longer holds its previous meaning for them, and ending the Islamic Republic's nuclear crisis has become the main issue. He added that the US seeks to reduce military war costs and the Islamic Republic can no longer use the threat of closing the Strait of Hormuz to reduce pressures as before.

Bijan Kian, a national security expert, said diplomatic negotiations between the US and the Islamic Republic could continue even after the start of military operations, but he believes Washington will not grant any concessions to the Iranian government. He also emphasized that external pressures alone will not be decisive and that the fate of the government will be determined by the Iranian people. Kian urged the families of soldiers not to allow their children to lose their lives in military operations.

Donald Trump said at a campaign rally in Mississippi that a small ceasefire was established with the Islamic Republic of Iran, which he considered a waste of time. He emphasized that Iran started the war and has been conducting hostile actions for years. Trump also said Iran had missiles that could reach Europe and that if no action was taken, American cities would have been targeted.

Nicholas Gilani, an investment banker in the US, said economic and financial pressures against the Islamic Republic will intensify in the coming weeks and the government's revenue will decrease. He added that the Islamic Republic might resort to the "madman theory" and deterrent war to disrupt calculations. Gilani also warned that increased pressures could worsen shortages of fuel, medicine, and essential goods, putting more strain on the Iranian people.

Three senior Israeli defense officials said Benjamin Netanyahu pressured for a new airstrike against the Islamic Republic in the weeks leading up to the election, but Eyal Zamir, the Chief of Staff, opposed it. Zamir believed there was no urgent need for action and opposed an attack before the election. The Israeli army said operational decisions are made solely based on security considerations.

US President Donald Trump said Washington had no choice but to attack the Islamic Republic and that Tehran had started the war. Referring to the killing of Qassem Soleimani, he added that the Islamic Republic has been targeting Americans since the 1979 revolution and previous US presidents should have acted sooner to stop the Iranian government.

Asia-Pacific media have covered the Israeli parliamentary elections focusing on the competition between Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eizenkot, the government's performance, and the country's political future. Meanwhile, media in India, Malaysia, and Hong Kong have addressed the threat from the Islamic Republic, Donald Trump's support for Netanyahu, and the regional consequences of the elections.

Shayan Samiei, a national security expert, said the Islamic Republic has been weakened after military strikes but still has the ability to create crises in the region. He stated that any agreement between the US and the Islamic Republic to end the crisis must include stopping Tehran's financial and arms support for its affiliated armed groups and controlling the routes of weapon transfers.

Kayhan newspaper wrote in an editorial that changing the nuclear doctrine and enhancing deterrence could prevent danger to the regime and territorial sovereignty of the country. The newspaper added that if the Islamic Republic had nuclear weapons, its leader would not have been attacked and assassinated in this way. Kayhan also referred to the deterrent role of nuclear weapons in the tensions between India and Pakistan and in North Korea.

Alaeddin Boroujerdi, a member of the National Security Commission of the Parliament, said that the missile and drone capabilities of the Islamic Republic are equivalent to a nuclear bomb. He added that Iran's missile stockpiles have increased by more than 50% and would not be depleted even if the war continues for two years. Boroujerdi also said that the Islamic Republic will not enter negotiations with the US without implementing its seven conditions, and if another war occurs, the response will be harsher and will cause damage to the entire region.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said in the Tuesday session of the Islamic Consultative Assembly that Mojtaba Khamenei is in full health and that what was very prominent and influential for him in meeting with him was his strong, lively, and hopeful spirit alongside his firmness and inner calm. Ghalibaf added that the leader's mastery over issues, both in general and in detail, was very remarkable. The speaker also said that during the session, various issues were discussed, including the country's economic matters, and Mojtaba Khamenei carefully followed macroeconomic indicators and emphasized the need for precise attention to these indicators.

Mansheh Amir, a Middle East expert, said that the formation of the next Israeli government may not be achieved even after weeks of negotiations and another election might be held. He also pointed to concerns about the Likud party possibly protesting the election results and disagreements over the assignment of the government formation mission.

Mohammad Javad Akbarin, a member of Iran International's editorial team, says officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey have traveled to Tehran to try to prevent the expansion of regional conflicts by relying on their defensive capacities and to influence the calculations of the Islamic Republic.

Seyed Mohammad Reza Razavi Fard, a lawyer, was summoned to serve a prison sentence. He was previously sentenced by the Revolutionary Court of Qom to 10 years and one day in prison. According to a notification dated 4 Aban, he was asked to appear within five days to execute the sentence.

The Tehran prosecutor has requested the approval and implementation of a resolution to completely ban men from all women's football matches by sending letters to the Minister of Sports and the Football Federation president. The prosecutor's office cited non-compliance with mandatory hijab and "moral norms and standards" as the reason for this action. This decision has faced strong protests from female players.
Yesterday, Paria Nasiri, a 17-year-old student from Naqadeh, was released on bail.

Fatemeh Mohajerani, the government spokesperson, stated that the government and other governing bodies are prepared for all possible scenarios and expressed confidence that "with unity, potential crises can be overcome." Mohajerani said the neither war nor peace situation harms the country and must be overcome. The spokesperson added that the government seeks peace with dignity but the armed forces will strongly defend the country if the slightest aggression occurs on its soil.

A video received by Iran International shows a group of students from Gorgan University of Natural Resources gathered on Tuesday, 5 Aban, in the presence of one of the university's deputies to protest the low quality of the cafeteria food.
